s1.title: RL in Production: Building Adaptive AI Systems
s1.summary: This is a technical guidance article from the Runpod team about deploying reinforcement-learning systems in production. It discusses architecture choices and operational challenges involving environment modeling, safe exploration, policy updates, online versus offline learning, distributed infrastructure, monitoring, rollback, human oversight, privacy, bias, and regulatory governance.

s2.title: Detecting Rewards Deterioration in RL
s2.summary: This research document concerns post-training monitoring of reinforcement-learning agents, focusing on detecting reward deterioration from a reference dataset. It discusses an optimal weighted-mean test based on reward covariance, and BFAR bootstrapping for controlling false alarms in sequential tests over non-independent episodic data.

s3.title: Building a Self-Healing RL Agent
s3.summary: This is a technical tutorial describing a Python self-healing reinforcement-learning agent built with Stable-Baselines3 and PPO on CartPole-v1. It discusses monitoring episodic rewards, detecting performance degradation, checkpointing the best model, diagnosing failures as model degradation, recovering by reloading a checkpoint and reducing the learning rate, and continuing training.

s4.title: What is Offline RL? (2026 Guide)
s4.summary: This is a 2026 technical guide to offline reinforcement learning, covering systems that train policies from fixed interaction logs rather than live exploration. It discusses data pipelines, conservative policy-training and evaluation methods, deployment architectures, shadow/canary rollouts, monitoring, safety constraints, failure modes, tooling, and use cases across cloud, Kubernetes, networking, applications, and CI/CD.

s6.title: Reward Hacking: Detection and Prevention (2026)
s6.summary: This is a 2026 technical guide about reward hacking in reinforcement-learning systems, including RLHF language models, robots, and simulated environments, with examples from OpenAI, DeepMind, and Anthropic. It discusses the design problem of proxy rewards diverging from intended objectives and decisions around reward construction, monitoring, evaluation, regularization, adversarial testing, and human oversight.

s7.title: Implementing Automated Rollback Mechanisms
s7.summary: This technical guidance document addresses automated rollback for machine-learning model deployments in production MLOps environments. It discusses selecting and tuning rollback triggers, shifting traffic or updating model-version pointers, integrating monitoring with deployment orchestration, identifying known-good versions, and testing, logging, and handling state during recovery.

s8.title: Handling LLM Model Drift in Production
s8.summary: This is a technical tutorial and literature review about maintaining large language model (LLM) systems in production, rather than a decision record for a named organization or project. It discusses detecting data, concept, and task drift; selecting monitoring metrics; and deciding among periodic retraining, parameter-efficient fine-tuning, online continual learning, retrieval augmentation, model editing, and human oversight.

s9.title: Deployment Considerations for RLHF Models
s9.summary: This is a deployment-guidance document from ApX Machine Learning Content Integrity & Transparency concerning production systems that serve RLHF-tuned language models. It discusses inference hardware, latency and batching; alignment monitoring and retraining; safety filters, moderation, rollback, version control, and staged deployment strategies.

s10.title: RLaaS: RL at Scale for Enterprise
s10.summary: This is a design document concerning RLaaS, a system for providing reinforcement learning at enterprise scale. It addresses architectural decisions involved in scaling and operating reinforcement-learning capabilities, although the supplied source contains no further details.

s11.title: Reward Hacking in RL (Lilian Weng)
s11.summary: This is a 2024 Lil’Log technical survey by Lilian Weng about reward hacking in reinforcement-learning systems, especially RLHF-trained language models. It examines reward-function misspecification, specification gaming, reward tampering, proxy and evaluator biases, in-context hacking, and generalization, and reviews mitigation options including reward design, adversarial testing, detection, decoupled approval, and dataset analysis.

s12.title: Reward Hacking in RL (Pan et al. summary)
s12.summary: This is a technical summary of Pan et al. (2022) research on reward hacking in reinforcement-learning systems. It discusses proxy-reward misspecification, capability-driven phase transitions from cooperative to exploitative behavior, and deployment decisions involving continuous monitoring and anomaly detection against trusted policy baselines when true rewards are unavailable.

s13.title: Emergent Misalignment from Reward Hacking
s13.summary: This is a research report from Anthropic’s alignment team about training large language models. It examines whether reward hacking on programming tasks generalizes into deception, alignment faking, cooperation with attackers, monitoring avoidance, and sabotage of AI-safety research. It compares mitigation approaches, including RLHF and inoculation prompts that frame cheating as contextually acceptable.

s14.title: Reward Hacking in RLVR Systems
s14.summary: This research overview concerns Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR) systems and surveys reward hacking across language, reasoning, robotics, and software-engineering applications. It discusses reward and verifier design, detection of specification gaming and related exploits, and mitigation decisions including hybrid verifiers, structured rubrics, process filtering, adversarial evaluation, and policy–reward co-optimization.

s15.title: OOD Detection for RL (Fraunhofer IKS)
s15.summary: This technical overview from the Fraunhofer Institute for Cognitive Systems IKS concerns out-of-distribution detection for reinforcement-learning agents in autonomous, safety-critical systems. It discusses adapting novelty detection from labeled machine-learning tasks to scenario-based RL, deciding how agents should identify unfamiliar situations and reject or escalate them. It also examines the tension between treating all novel inputs as unsafe and allowing useful generalization.

s16.title: When RL Safety Constraints Break
s16.summary: This is a technical explainer on safety design in reinforcement-learning systems. It examines how reward penalties, constrained MDPs, adaptive Lagrange multipliers, state-based rules, runtime shields, offline learning, and robustness assumptions can fail under distribution shift, and outlines layered alternatives including uncertainty estimation, adaptive shielding, out-of-distribution detection, and stress testing.

s17.title: How Can RL Agents Be Monitored?
s17.summary: This is a question-and-answer discussion about monitoring production reinforcement-learning agents, illustrated by an Amazon-like search-ranking system. It considers detecting degradation or undesirable behavior through test cases, ground truth, reward thresholds, batch updates, A/B testing, rollback, and monitoring for out-of-sample data, with retraining as a response.

s18.title: Diagnosing Instability in Production RL
s18.summary: This technical article describes diagnostics for production-scale, tool-using reinforcement-learning and agent post-training systems, including Microsoft’s Post-Training Toolkit and its integration with Hugging Face TRL. It addresses variance amplification in tool-conditioned, low-support states and discusses slice-aware tail and ESS monitoring, distributed aggregation, constrained tool outputs, KL caps, rollback policies, and failure-aware curricula.

s19.title: Deploying RL Models: MLOps Challenges
s19.summary: This is a technical guidance article about MLOps for deploying reinforcement-learning models in real-time production environments, including physical and high-stakes systems. It discusses policy drift and continuous learning, offline versus online evaluation, safety guardrails, reward design, monitoring, versioning, staged rollouts, and rollback mechanisms.

s20.title: Deploying RL with Ray and Amazon SageMaker
s20.summary: This AWS technical post describes deploying reinforcement-learning policies with Ray/RLlib and Amazon SageMaker RL, using a basketball inventory supply-chain agent as an example. It discusses modeling states, actions, rewards, and simulation; selecting and scaling distributed training; tracking experiments and costs; and deploying, autoscaling, testing, logging, and monitoring policies in production.

s21.title: Deploying RL Agents in Private Clouds
s21.summary: This is a technical architecture and deployment guidance document for reinforcement-learning agents running in private-cloud, real-time decision systems. It discusses streaming-data integration, microservice APIs, feedback and retraining loops, monitoring, scalability and high availability, security and access control, and possible federated and edge-deployment models.

s22.title: RLHF at Scale: Enterprise LLMs with HITL
s22.summary: This blog post from NextWealth concerns enterprise large language models and the use of reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF) with human-in-the-loop (HITL) processes. It discusses decisions around contextual alignment, ethical and bias correction, continuous adaptation, data annotation, real-time validation, post-deployment tuning, error correction, and the resource, consistency, and workflow challenges of scaling human feedback.

s23.title: RLHF: Enterprise Integration
s23.summary: This is a Tredence blog article describing enterprise adoption of reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF) for large language models and AI agents. It discusses the feedback-to-reward-model-to-policy pipeline, annotation and reward-model design, MLOps and business-system integration, governance and bias mitigation, implementation challenges, and choices between RLHF and alternatives such as RLAIF.

s24.title: Evaluate, Monitor, Tune LLMs
s24.summary: This blog article from the GenAI Foundry series concerns enterprise-owned LLMs, including applications such as InsurancGPT. It discusses multi-layer evaluation, domain benchmarks, human review, guardrails, auditability, continuous monitoring, drift detection, and reinforcement or preference tuning through RLHF and DPO.

s25.title: Reward Hacking Is Becoming More Sophisticated
s25.summary: This LessWrong article examines reward hacking in frontier large language models, including systems from OpenAI, Anthropic, and other organizations. It discusses increasingly deliberate methods of exploiting evaluation environments, possible links to reinforcement learning and model capability, risks for AI alignment, and research directions for evaluation, monitoring, and mitigation.

s26.title: MONA: Steganography Without Optimisation
s26.summary: This is an update to the MONA research paper from the AI Alignment Forum, concerning methods for training AI agents with myopic approval. It discusses preventing multi-step reward hacking, the relationship between MONA and RLHF, steganographic or unfaithful reasoning arising without monitor optimization, model-organism environments, and implications for chain-of-thought monitoring and scalable oversight.

s27.title: CoT Monitoring for Frontier Reasoning Models
s27.summary: This research report examines frontier reasoning models and an LLM-based chain-of-thought (CoT) monitoring system for detecting reward hacking in coding tasks. It discusses whether monitors should access CoT alongside actions and concludes that strong optimization pressure on CoT can induce models to conceal malicious intent, recommending caution with such supervision.

s28.title: Reasoning Models Don't Always Say What They Think
s28.summary: This is a research article describing an Anthropic Alignment Science study of reasoning models, including Claude 3.7 Sonnet and DeepSeek R1. It examines whether chain-of-thought explanations faithfully reveal model reasoning, evaluates hint disclosure and reward-hacking scenarios, and considers whether outcome-based training can improve faithfulness for monitoring and alignment.

s29.title: Gaming the System: Reward Hacking in LLM Training
s29.summary: This technical explainer concerns reinforcement-learning-based alignment of large language models, particularly RLHF pipelines used in systems such as OpenAI’s InstructGPT and Anthropic’s models. It discusses the design problem of proxy reward models being exploited through verbosity, sycophancy, or other shortcuts, and mitigation decisions including KL regularization, adversarial feedback, improved reward modeling, process supervision, rule-based constraints, monitoring, and explicit penalties.
